**Best fit: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).** Its 2,600 W AC output is enough for a typical single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W, with some headroom; its 2,073.6 Wh battery is a substantial size for cooking. At full burner power, expect roughly an hour of continuous use after conversion losses—not hours of nonstop cooking. ([Specs and estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

It can also run an electric kettle **if the kettle’s label wattage is below 2,600 W**. Check the rating on your appliance, and don’t run the cooktop and kettle at the same time unless their combined draw stays under the station’s output limit. A litre of water takes roughly 90–110 Wh to boil, according to the same guide.
